title: Johnny Lala and the 50-piece Italian parade band
summary: Talk of Johnny Lala, who played Schilling's band and stayed home rather than go to New York, and of the Italian band in uniform playing parades.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: I'm trying to think of the guys from the French Quarter then. Who was that? Johnny Lala was around? Was he with you to? Well, Johnny Lala didn't play with the Italian band, no.
He played with just like Valley Hoon, dances and all that stuff. Yeah. He played with Schilling band for a long time.

Well, he was... The guy was supposed to go with what's called Dixieland Band, to New York, see. But he wouldn't go because he had a meat market with his dad. And so he says, no, I can make more money here. But he was a better trumpet player than Nick, you know. I mean, he moved the band. That's what they said. So... Like, see, Johnny Lala was known, uh... Oh, man. They must have had a lot of good musicians, you know, probably. Well, all the Brunner's boys played good. That's the boy that I work with all the time. Jack Lane, you know. You heard of Jack Lane. Pansy Lane, Jack Lane's son. But like I said, there's Italian band.
Just Tony Fernand and I that came out of the band. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.

Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. 50 piece band. We used to play all these parades, you know. And we used to wear those Italian uniforms. I mean, it was really Italian band though. I've seen pictures of the old ones,
you know. Oh you didn't? I think like some parade, like Contessa Antiglia, would be posed in front of the church. And they'd all line up in front of the church.
